query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy coatings, enhanced high-temperature wear resistance and reduced microscopic deformation during sliding are governed by the in-situ formation and self-replenishment of a Cu-rich oxide tribofilm, which forms more effectively when oxygen is available.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate with a baseline microstructure and thickness, prepared without intentional modifications to promote oxidation.
generation.intervention: Systematically vary the oxygen partial pressure in the sliding environment—from near-vacuum to ambient air—while keeping coating thickness, microstructure, load, sliding speed, and temperature constant.
generation.conditions: Sliding wear tests conducted at high temperatures between 600 °C and 900 °C under controlled oxygen partial pressure conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: A Cu-rich oxide tribofilm that forms on the coating surface during high-temperature sliding.
generation.mechanism: Under high oxygen partial pressure, Cu in the alloy oxidizes at the sliding interface to form a protective tribofilm. This oxide layer reduces direct metal-to-metal contact and limits plastic deformation by acting as a lubricious and resilient barrier, thereby enhancing wear resistance during high-temperature sliding.
generation.predicted_outcome: Coatings tested in ambient air (with higher oxygen partial pressure) will develop a thicker, more continuous Cu-rich oxide tribofilm, leading to lower wear rates and reduced microscopic deformation compared to coatings tested in near-vacuum conditions.
generation.baseline: FeNiCrCoCu coating tested under minimal oxygen (near-vacuum) conditions at temperatures between 600 °C and 900 °C, where less protective oxidation is expected.
generation.boundary: This mechanism is predicted to dominate wear behavior in the high-temperature regime (600–900 °C); its influence at lower temperatures is uncertain due to slower oxidation kinetics.
generation.uncertainty: The detailed kinetics and long-term stability of the Cu-rich oxide tribofilm under dynamic sliding conditions are not fully understood, and additional microstructural analyses are needed to clarify the self-replenishment behavior of the oxide layer.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct high-temperature sliding wear tests (600–900 °C) under two controlled environments: one with near-vacuum oxygen levels and another with ambient air. Characterize the surface after sliding using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) to assess tribofilm formation, and measure wear rates and plastic deformation using profilometry and microscopy.
measurements: Quantitative wear rate (material loss per sliding distance)
Surface morphology and thickness of oxide tribofilm (via SEM/EDS)
Microscopic analysis of plastic deformation features (via optical/SEM imaging)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If increasing the oxygen partial pressure does not result in a detectable, continuous Cu-rich oxide tribofilm, or if no significant reduction in wear rate and microscopic deformation is observed compared to near-vacuum conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.

The purpose of this work is to investigate the effect of the Cr content on the microstructure and properties of the WVTaTiCr x coating. The morphologies and phase compositions of five coatings with different Cr contents were comparatively observed. In addition, the hardness and high-temperature oxidation resistance of the coatings were also analyzed. As a result, with the increase in Cr, the coating grains were more refined. All the coating is mainly composed of the BCC solid-solution phase, which promotes the precipitation of the Laves phase with the increase in Cr. The addition of Cr greatly improves the hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and corrosion resistance of the coating. The WVTaTiCr (Cr 1 ) exhibited superior mechanical properties, especially in terms of its exceptional hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and outstanding corrosion resistance. Abstract In this paper, the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating was prepared on MoNbTaTiW RHEA by a fused slurry method. The microstructural evolution and compositions of the silicide coating under high-temperature oxidation environment were studied. The results show that the silicide coating could effectively prevent the oxidation of the MoNbTaTiW RHEA. The initial silicide coating had a double-layer structure: a high silicon content layer mainly composed of MSi 2 as the outer layer and a low silicon content layer mainly contained M 5 Si 3 as the inner layer. Under high-temperature oxidation conditions, the silicon element diffused from the silicide coating to the RHEA substrate while the oxidation of the coating occurred. After oxidation, the coating was composed of an outer oxide layer and an inner silicide layer. The silicide layer moved toward the inside of the substrate, led to the increase of its thickness. Compared with the initial silicified layer, its structure did not change significantly. The structure and compositions of the oxide layer on the outer surface strongly depended on the oxidation temperature. decision.trend: Recent studies on high-entropy alloy coatings highlight that forming stable oxide-based tribofilms at moderate-to-high temperatures can substantially reduce wear. In 2019 (PMC7515071), an AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 coating demonstrated that spinel oxide layers emerging above ~800 °C significantly improved wear resistance. In 2020 (PMC7304825), a CuMoTaWV refractory high-entropy alloy film showed that nanocrystalline structure and post-deposition treatments enhanced tribological performance at elevated temperatures. These works suggest that oxidation-driven tribofilm formation, combined with stable microstructures, can be key to superior high-temperature wear behavior—yet the dominant controlling mechanism remains unresolved for FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
decision.unsolved: While oxide tribofilms have been linked to enhanced wear resistance in several high-entropy alloys at high temperatures, it is unclear if and how a protective oxide layer governs both the overall wear rate and microscopic plastic deformation in FeNiCrCoCu coatings. The interplay among elemental partitioning, in-situ oxide formation, microstructural evolution, and substrate interactions is not fully understood, particularly above ~600 °C where diffusion and oxidation kinetics accelerate.
decision.lever: Systematically vary the oxygen partial pressure in the high-temperature sliding environment (from near-vacuum to air) while maintaining the baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating thickness, microstructure, and test parameters (load, speed, temperature).
decision.why: We hypothesize that the key mechanism governing wear and microscopic deformation at temperatures above ~600 °C is the formation and self-replenishment of a Cu-rich oxide tribofilm on the FeNiCrCoCu coating surface. Prior work (PMC7515071, PMC7304825) shows that such oxide films can form in related high-entropy alloys under heat and stress, substantially reducing wear. By altering the oxygen partial pressure from near-vacuum to air, one can assess whether the presence and stability of this tribofilm are indeed crucial. In higher-oxygen environments, thicker oxide scales should form, lowering the wear rate and limiting plastic deformation in the 600–900 °C regime. If wear remains high or if no oxide tribofilm forms despite adequate oxygen, this outcome would falsify the proposed hypothesis.
